notes: All three case kinds (LAWSUIT, STAY_OBJECTION, VERDICT) live in one case_file table distinguished by case_kind, per the shared design brief; parent_case_id and origin_case_id are kept as two separate self-referencing FK columns (not merged) because they are semantically distinct: parent_case_id is a mandatory spawn-time link (max 1 child per parent, enforced by UNIQUE(parent_case_id), Postgres allows multiple NULLs so this does not restrict non-stay cases), while origin_case_id is an optional many-to-one reference link chosen by search at verdict intake with no uniqueness constraint.

Court case numbers (courtName, blackCaseNo, redCaseNo, courtSarabanNo, paccCaseNo, centralSarabanNo, lawReceiveNo, verdictNoticeNo/Date) are single-valued per case row in every seed example found in §6.1 of the extraction, so they were kept directly on case_file rather than a 1:N child table; the stay-objection child may still override courtName locally since it has its own case_file row.

l3DirectorOrderNotes / l3GroupAssignNotes / l3GroupApproveNotes / l3AnswerGroupReview / l3AnswerDirectorReview / l3AnswerReturn and their l7/l8/l9/l9a/l9b/l10 equivalents are all overwritten in place in the source mockup (a known gap noted in §4: "overwritten per step in mockup -> normalise to 1:N history"). This design fixes that gap by routing all assignment/order notes through the generic case_assignment table and all review/return/reject notes through the generic case_review table, both keyed by (case_id, phase_code, step_code, round_no) so every send-back round is preserved instead of lost on resubmission (the l3AnswerReturn: undefined clear-on-resubmit pattern in the source).

Generic reuse tables (signature, attachment, document_number, case_assignment, case_review, case_draft_opinion, postal_dispatch, phase_intake, case_close) are shared across phases via a phase_code/step_code column rather than one bespoke table per page, per the design brief and to keep the table count near the ~35 budget for this, the largest of the three activities (final count: 32 tables).

Part 9 (l9Board* — board_propose_result table: meeting date, resolution no, decision APPEAL/NO_APPEAL, notes) is modeled per the task brief instruction, but per extraction §2/§6.1 this data exists only as seed/demo data in the mockup — no page in the 10.3 flow actually writes these fields (only 01-work-inbox reads l9BoardDecision for a badge). Flagged here as an explicit source gap rather than invented business logic.

l3ExtensionNotes (a single case-level note accompanying the whole batch of l3ExtensionRequests[]) is stored on answer_document_set instead of a dedicated table, because the source mockup writes both in the same Activity103.advance() call at 10-3-13; extension_request itself is normalised to one row per round_no (fixing the source array-overwrite pattern) instead of a single overwritten object.

attachment carries an optional extension_request_id FK (nullable) so that per-round extension-order files can stay attributable to a specific round; this is a deliberate small extension of the otherwise generic (case_id, step_code, doc_type) attachment shape, since the source itself only loosely associates files with a round via an in-memory JS array index.

document_number gained two generic extra columns (urgency, forward_to_role) beyond the design brief's baseline shape, to hold the ชั้นความเร็ว (urgency) and routing captured only at the registry external-number step (10-3-20, l3AnswerUrgency/l3AnswerRegistryForwardTo); both are nullable and unused for internal/registration numbers.

case_close is keyed by case_id alone (not case_id+phase_code) because within the scope of this extraction each case (main lawsuit, verdict case, or stay-objection child) is only ever closed once — the lawsuit case itself never reaches its own close step in-flow (it stays at L3_AWAITING_JUDGMENT until a separate VERDICT case is created), the verdict case closes via either the VERDICT_STEPS CLOSE branch or the board-no-appeal (l9b) branch (mutually exclusive paths on the same case), and the stay-objection child closes via its own l3StayCloseNotes. The close_notes column is documented as sourced from whichever of l3CloseNotes / l3StayCloseNotes / l9bCloseNotes applies.

Attachment file arrays are stored as filename-only rows (no bytes/storage), matching the source mockup which validates and stores only file names client-side; storage_key/mime_type/size_bytes columns are added as standard technical columns for a real implementation and are nullable.

Signing method (hand-drawn PAD vs. CERT certificate stamp) is inferred from the presence of a certId in each page's signature modal config (e.g. "PACC-DIRLEGAL-2569-103"); the mockup itself only ever stores the resulting image, so sign_method/cert_id are the DB's explicit normalisation of that modal choice.

01-work-inbox.html mock rows for type "10.3" (§6.2) are list-only demo objects with a different, legacy status vocabulary (PENDING_DIRECTOR, DRAFTING_OPINION, etc.) that never appear in the real §5 STEPS tables; they were excluded from the status/step lookups as out-of-scope UI demo data, not real workflow state.

stay_objection child's chairman-sign-step notes (l3StayObjectionChairmanNotes) were folded into the generic case_review table (phase_code=STAY_OBJECTION, step_code=LAW0098) rather than a bespoke stay_objection_detail table, since the field is semantically identical to every other reviewer/signer notes field already generalised there.

Legacy 10.1-schema duplicate fields written by 02-board-intake for non-10.3 categories (source, docNo, prosecutorCaseType*, offenseBases, summary, legalOpinion, blackNo, redNo, courtOrder, accuser/accused) are out of scope for this 10.3 schema — they are dead columns on shared-mockup case objects, hidden by the page's own category branching, and not part of the คดีศาลปกครอง business data model.
